exponent_audit.justification: √(d/(εp))=O(ε) is equivalent to ε³=Ω(d/p); the additive 16/p is absorbed when εp=Ω(1), which holds in the legal cubic regime.

Every Sylvester monomial is bihomogeneous of coefficient-degrees s₀ and r₀ and has total Z-index r₀s₀, giving base degree at most s₀u+r₀v−dr₀s₀. A common formal graph makes its base line divide the nonzero resultant.

Because F_p is perfect, the distinct absolute factors form one Frobenius orbit. Frobenius preserves support, so each has weight δ/k and Z-degree r/k. Applying P2 to two conjugates gives the exact first bound; (δ−dr)²≥0 gives the remaining inequalities.

Primitivity excludes base-only factors. Assigning each supported line to a factor and using Σδ_i²≤(Σδ_i)²≤D² proves the union bound. For C=Z²−νH₀², nonsquareness of ν in F_p(t) excludes every graph outside the d factors of H₀.

At B_Z=0, the differentiated graph identity requires (B_X,B_Y)·v_L=0. Smoothness makes this a nonzero functional on F_p², with one projective kernel direction and hence at most one accepted edge above each base point.

D<2d forces B=aZ+b. Coprimality over F_p persists geometrically: any common absolute factor would bring its full Frobenius orbit and yield an F_p common divisor. Gauss and Bézout then prove absolute irreducibility and the D(D−d) bound, including constant/zero coefficient cases.

The Y-adic valuation of XYg² is odd, so it is not a square over the algebraic closure's rational function field; the quadratic is absolutely irreducible. Substitution verifies every graph, the slope count exceeds D, and all d ramified lifts per graph have zero full gradient.

literature_audit.claim: KTZ Theorem 1.1 and the cited bivariate constants
literature_audit.justification: Revision 1 states the cubic threshold over every finite field, outputs one total-degree-at-most-d polynomial, and its bivariate proof concludes ε/8000. Lemmas 3.2 and 4.1 give the stated reference and D bounds.

Section 2.5 defines the resultant through the Sylvester determinant and calls Res_z(A,A_z) the z-discriminant. Lemma 3.1 assumes a squarefree specialized fiber, and its proof invokes Newton lifting at a simple root. The paper formulates a best-fit oracle, but replacing an arbitrary supplied label by a best fit cannot decrease acceptance; no quantitative HKSS theorem is imported here.

Theorem 34 bounds affine substitutions yielding a local z-linear factor when no corresponding global factor exists. Lemma 35 and Corollary 36 implement the squarefree/discriminant step. The submission correctly flags separability as mathematically necessary and uses none of these results quantitatively.
For an absolutely irreducible projective plane curve of degree r, the corollary gives the stated Weil bound with (r−1)(r−2)√p, including singular curves.

The lemma bounds rational points of an F_q-irreducible but non-absolutely-irreducible variety by a degree-squared, codimension-one-scale term; the curve description is a valid specialization. The new purification theorem is independently proved and does not rely on this estimate.

The controlling quantifier is prime p and integer 101≤d<p, exactly equivalent to 100<d<p. No proof or sanity check invokes d≤100.

Every new object and graph identity is over F_p. Absolute factors are used only inside algebraic closure for geometric irreducibility and Frobenius comparison; no extension-field line test or descent conclusion appears.

All base polynomials use X,Y, every graph is an affine line in F_p², the line-factor argument is bivariate, and P5's unique-kernel-direction conclusion is specifically two-dimensional. No dimension lift is used.

For every F_p-irreducible Z-dependent C and every distinct family of formal degree-d graphs, Frobenius transitivity and P2 prove the stated bound without an unstated D<p, separability, or smoothness assumption.
The fixed-factor and smooth-lift hypotheses are essential and explicit. The bound counts only accepted incidences from graph lines of that factor and is uniform over all point and line tables.

For every d≤D<2d and primitive Z-dependent B of weight at most D, the proof handles all coefficient degeneracies and bounds the F_p ramified base set. At D=d the bound is zero and the leading coefficient is constant.

For every legal 101≤d≤p−2, there are enough distinct c_j and, when needed, b; D=d+1<p. The inequality sp>D follows from s≥51 and p>D. The excluded endpoint d=p−1 is separately and correctly analyzed, not silently claimed.

The construction proves formal graph identities. Even if 'matches a label' were read only pointwise, both restrictions have degree below p, so agreement on all p line points implies formal equality before P9's line-factor argument.

This obstruction claim asserts no positive soundness theorem or list output. Its stated global conclusion is the exact nonexistence of one total-degree-at-most-d polynomial matching all selected labels, and P9 proves precisely that; it does not silently replace this with a weaker root statement.
Purification and residual-deletion consequences are expressly conditional architecture diagnostics, not universal asymptotic theorems or lower bounds on every interpolant.
The p=103 and p=409 computations are legal-regime falsification checks only. Every quantified result is supported symbolically, so finite experiments are not used to certify asymptotic quantifiers.

summary: Accept the exact SHA-identified obstruction claim. Every algebraic bound, incidence normalization, construction, characteristic condition, and quantifier verifies in dimension m=2 over prime F_p for all integers 100<d<p, with clause (iv) correctly restricted to d≤p−2 and the endpoint separately handled. P9 proves the exact one-polynomial nonexistence conclusion. No soundness exponent is claimed or improved: because d/p<1, an exponent greater than 1/3 would be stronger, while this submission leaves the unconditional benchmark at 1/3.
